slots.default: Cardiff in particular

slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: What we account for in Cardiff

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Cardiff carries a mix most cities do not: a substantial public-sector and public-adjacent economy, a media production cluster, and a financial services presence. It also brings a genuine technical requirement almost nowhere else in our coverage does.

slots.label: Heading 2
slots.default: Welsh language is a configuration requirement, not a preference

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: Organisations delivering public-facing services in Wales may have obligations to offer Welsh alongside English. In IT terms that reaches into templates, signatures, forms, website content and sometimes keyboard and locale settings. It is far easier to build in at setup than to retrofit across a live estate.

slots.label: Heading 3
slots.default: Public-sector adjacency raises the assurance bar

slots.label: Paragraph 8
slots.default: Suppliers to Welsh public bodies are often asked to evidence security controls in a formal questionnaire rather than a conversation. Having documented answers on access control, retention and incident response ready in advance saves weeks on a tender.

slots.label: Heading 4
slots.default: Media production moves large files on deadlines

slots.label: Paragraph 11
slots.default: Video and audio work generates volumes that ordinary office broadband and ordinary backup windows were not sized for. The practical answers are staged local storage, sensible sync rules and being honest about what a connection can actually carry.

slots.label: Heading 5
slots.default: Onsite attendance is scheduled, and we say so

slots.label: Paragraph 14
slots.default: Engineers travel from London and Stevenage, so a Cardiff visit is planned rather than immediate. We would rather state that plainly than list a virtual Cardiff address and imply otherwise. Remote resolution handles most of what arises, and we plan onsite work around genuine need.

slots.label: Heading 6
slots.default: Operating either side of the border

slots.label: Paragraph 17
slots.default: Businesses based in Cardiff frequently trade across England and Wales, which can mean two sets of public-sector frameworks, procurement portals and language expectations to satisfy from a single IT estate. Designing for both at the outset avoids maintaining two half-solutions.

slots.label: Heading 7
slots.default: Broadcast and production deadlines narrow the change window

slots.label: Paragraph 20
slots.default: When output is scheduled, maintenance cannot simply happen on a convenient evening. Work has to fit around transmission and delivery commitments, which means agreeing windows in advance and having a tested way back if a change misbehaves. The alternative, deferring everything until it is urgent, is how organisations end up doing risky work at the worst possible moment.

slots.label: Heading 8
slots.default: Contributors who are not employees still need access

slots.label: Paragraph 23
slots.default: Production work brings in freelancers, contributors and post houses who need particular material for a defined period. Handling that through named, time-limited access to specific content, rather than broad shares or files passed around, keeps control of the material and makes it possible to say precisely who could reach what. It is also markedly easier than trying to recall a link that has already been forwarded.
